question: Suppose the market demand for artisan bread is given by Qd = 150 - 5P and the market supply is given by Qs = 30 + 10P. What is the equilibrium quantity traded in this market?
explain: Equilibrium occurs where Qd = Qs, so 150 - 5P = 30 + 10P, which yields 15P = 120 and P = 8. Substituting P = 8 back into demand gives Qd = 150 - 5(8) = 110 units.

biz.text: I run a bakery. Demand for our bread is Qd = 150 − 5P and supply is Qs = 30 + 10P. How many units are traded when the market clears?
biz.say: We will produce and sell {v} units.

concept: Shifts in Demand vs Movements Along Curve
question: Which of the following events will cause a rightward shift in the demand curve for traditional leather shoes?
options: A decrease in the price of traditional leather shoes
An increase in consumer income, assuming leather shoes are a normal good
An increase in the cost of leather used for manufacturing
A decrease in consumer income, assuming leather shoes are a normal good
explain: An increase in consumer income increases the demand for normal goods, shifting the entire demand curve to the right. A price change causes a movement along the curve, while production costs affect supply.

biz.text: I want to forecast next season for my leather shoe shop. Which of these events will shift the demand curve for traditional leather shoes to the right?

question: In the market for organic coffee, market demand is represented by Qd = 200 - 10P and market supply is represented by Qs = 50 + 5P. What is the equilibrium price?
explain: Set Qd equal to Qs: 200 - 10P = 50 + 5P. Rearranging terms gives 150 = 15P, which results in P = 10.

biz.text: I distribute organic coffee. Demand is Qd = 200 − 10P and supply is Qs = 50 + 5P. What is the market-clearing price?

question: What happens in a competitive market when a binding price ceiling is imposed below the equilibrium price?
options: A surplus is created because quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded
A shortage is created because quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied
Equilibrium is automatically restored through price adjustments
Supply shifts to the right to eliminate the price difference
explain: A binding price ceiling set below the equilibrium price keeps prices artificially low, leading consumers to demand more while producers supply less, resulting in a market shortage.

biz.text: The city wants to cap rents below the market equilibrium rate. In a competitive market, what happens when a binding price ceiling is imposed below the equilibrium price?

question: Given market demand Qd = 300 - 20P and market supply Qs = 60 + 10P, what is the magnitude of the market shortage if a price ceiling is imposed at P = 5?
explain: At P = 5, Qd = 300 - 20(5) = 200 and Qs = 60 + 10(5) = 110. The shortage is Qd - Qs = 200 - 110 = 90 units.

biz.text: The city fixed our tool prices at 5 dollars. Demand is Qd = 300 − 20P and supply is Qs = 60 + 10P. How big is the shortage, in units?
biz.say: There is a shortage of {v} units.

question: Which of the following best describes the economic intuition behind the Law of Supply?
options: Consumers are willing to buy more units only when household income increases.
Higher prices provide an incentive for firms to expand production and for new firms to enter the market.
Higher production costs automatically lead to lower market prices.
Suppliers reduce output when prices increase to conserve scarce resources.
explain: The Law of Supply states that higher prices increase the profitability of production, incentivizing existing firms to produce more and new firms to enter, creating a positive relationship between price and quantity supplied.

biz.text: A new hire asked me why higher prices make firms produce more. Which of these best describes the economic intuition behind the Law of Supply?

question: For a regional bicycle market with demand Qd = 500 - 15P and supply Qs = 100 + 5P, what is the size of the surplus if a price floor is established at P = 25?
explain: At P = 25, Qd = 500 − 15(25) = 125 and Qs = 100 + 5(25) = 225. The surplus is Qs − Qd = 225 − 125 = 100 units (the floor of 25 is above the equilibrium price of 20, so it binds).

biz.text: A price floor pushed bicycle prices up to 25 dollars. Demand is Qd = 500 − 15P and supply is Qs = 100 + 5P. How many units are left unsold?
biz.say: We are left with {v} unsold units.

concept: Simultaneous Shifts in Supply and Demand
question: If the demand for a product increases while its supply decreases simultaneously, what can be predicted with certainty about the new market equilibrium?
options: The equilibrium price will rise, but the effect on equilibrium quantity is ambiguous.
The equilibrium quantity will rise, but the effect on equilibrium price is ambiguous.
Both equilibrium price and quantity will decrease.
Both equilibrium price and quantity will increase.
explain: An increase in demand pushes price and quantity up, while a decrease in supply pushes price up and quantity down. Combining these shifts means the equilibrium price rises unambiguously, whereas the net effect on quantity depends on the relative magnitudes of the shifts.

biz.text: For my commodity report: if demand for a product increases while its supply decreases at the same time, what can I predict with certainty about the new equilibrium?

concept: Effect of Supply Shift on Equilibrium Price
question: Initial demand is Qd = 200 − 5P and initial supply is Qs = 50 + 5P. A supply shock shifts supply to Qs = 30 + 5P. What is the new equilibrium price?
explain: Set demand equal to the new supply: 200 − 5P = 30 + 5P, so 170 = 10P and P = 17.

biz.text: Demand is Qd = 200 − 5P and supply was Qs = 50 + 5P, but a supply shock moved supply to Qs = 30 + 5P. What is the new equilibrium price?
biz.say: The new equilibrium price is {v} dollars.

question: Which of the following is a defining assumption of a perfectly competitive market?
options: Firms have significant market power to influence the market price.
Products offered by competing sellers are highly differentiated.
There are many buyers and sellers, making everyone a price taker.
Government intervention is required to set daily market prices.
explain: Perfect competition requires a large number of buyers and sellers trading identical products, ensuring that no individual market participant has the power to influence the market price (price takers).

biz.text: For my study of grain markets: which of these is a defining assumption of a perfectly competitive market?

question: If the market demand function is given by Qd = 240 - 8P, what is the quantity demanded when the market price is set at P = 15?
explain: Substitute P = 15 into the demand equation: Qd = 240 - 8(15) = 240 - 120 = 120 units.

biz.text: Our demand formula is Qd = 240 − 8P and our pricing team set the price at 15 dollars. How many units will consumers demand?

question: What are the two primary functions of prices in a market economy?
options: To maximize government tax revenue and eliminate inflation
To act as a selection device and convey information
To guarantee equal income distribution and eliminate scarcity
To control production quotas and enforce trade agreements
explain: Prices serve as a rationing/selection device (allocating goods to those who value them most) and as a transmission mechanism for information about relative scarcity.

biz.text: A journalist asked me what prices actually do in a market economy. What are the two primary functions of prices?

question: A consumer's linear demand curve generates a maximum willingness to pay of $100 at zero quantity. If the market price is fixed at $40 and the equilibrium quantity purchased is 60 units, what is the total consumer surplus?
explain: Consumer surplus is calculated as the area of the triangle below demand and above price: 0.5 * base * height = 0.5 * 60 units * ($100 - $40) = 0.5 * 60 * 60 = $1,800.

biz.text: Our customers would pay at most 100 dollars. The market price is 40 dollars and 60 units are sold. What is the total consumer surplus, in dollars?
biz.say: The total consumer surplus is {v} dollars.

question: If the price elasticity of demand for a good is estimated to be -2.5, how should this demand be classified?
options: Inelastic, meaning quantity demanded changes proportionately less than price
Elastic, meaning quantity demanded is highly responsive to percentage changes in price
Unit elastic, meaning total revenue remains constant when price changes
Perfectly inelastic, meaning quantity demanded is entirely unresponsive to price
explain: An absolute price elasticity greater than 1 (| -2.5 | > 1) means demand is elastic, indicating that the percentage change in quantity demanded exceeds the percentage change in price.

biz.text: Our market research estimates a price elasticity of demand of −2.5 for our product. How should we classify this demand?

concept: Price Elasticity of Demand Percentage Calculation
question: When the price of a designer handbag rises from $200 to $240 (a 20% increase), the quantity demanded drops from 50 units to 35 units. What is the absolute value of the percentage drop in quantity demanded?
explain: Percentage change in quantity = [(35 - 50) / 50] * 100 = (-15 / 50) * 100 = -30%, so the absolute percentage drop is 30%.

biz.text: We raised the price of our designer handbag by 20 percent, from $200 to $240, and sales fell from 50 to 35 units. By what percent did the quantity demanded fall?

question: Which of the following factors tends to make the demand for a specific good more elastic?
options: The good is an absolute necessity with no close substitutes.
The time horizon considered is very short.
The product represents a large share of the consumer's total budget and has many close substitutes.
The good is narrowly defined as a habit-forming addictive substance.
explain: Goods that absorb a large budget share and have many available substitutes feature more elastic demand because consumers can easily switch when prices change.

biz.text: Which of these factors tends to make the demand for a good more elastic?

question: A consumer has a weekly entertainment budget of $120. If concert tickets cost $30 each and movie tickets cost $15 each, what is the maximum number of movie tickets the consumer can purchase if they buy 2 concert tickets?
explain: Spending on 2 concert tickets = 2 * $30 = $60. Remaining budget for movie tickets = $120 - $60 = $60. Maximum movie tickets = $60 / $15 = 4 units.

biz.text: I have 120 dollars for entertainment. Concert tickets cost 30 dollars and movie tickets 15 dollars. I buy 2 concert tickets. How many movie tickets can I afford at most?

question: If the income elasticity of demand for a particular vacation package is calculated to be +1.8, how is this good classified?
options: An inferior good
A normal and luxury good
A normal and necessity good
A Giffen good
explain: A positive income elasticity greater than 1 indicates that demand increases faster than income, classifying the item as a normal luxury good.

biz.text: Our models show an income elasticity of demand of +1.8 for a vacation package. How is this good classified?

question: If the cross-price elasticity of demand between product A and product B is negative (-1.2), how are the two products related?
options: They are substitutes
They are complements
They are independent goods
They are inferior goods
explain: A negative cross-price elasticity indicates that when the price of product B rises, the demand for product A falls, meaning consumers use them together as complements.

biz.text: The cross-price elasticity of demand between product A and product B is −1.2. How are the two products related?

question: When the price of streaming subscriptions increases by 10%, the quantity demanded for smart TVs falls by 25%. What is the cross-price elasticity of demand between streaming subscriptions and smart TVs?
explain: Cross-price elasticity = (% change in quantity of smart TVs) / (% change in price of subscriptions) = -25% / 10% = -2.5.

biz.text: A 10 percent rise in streaming fees led to a 25 percent drop in smart TV sales. What is the cross-price elasticity of demand?

question: If a firm faces an elastic demand curve for its product, what will happen to total revenue if the firm decreases its price?
options: Total revenue will decrease
Total revenue will increase
Total revenue will remain unchanged
Total revenue will drop to zero
explain: When demand is elastic, the percentage increase in quantity demanded outweighs the percentage decrease in price, causing total revenue to rise when price is lowered.

biz.text: Our demand is elastic. If we decrease our price, what will happen to our total revenue?

question: A firm's supply curve has a vertical intercept at a price of $10. If the market equilibrium price is $50 and the equilibrium quantity supplied is 40 units, what is the total producer surplus?
explain: Producer surplus is calculated as the area of the triangle above supply and below price: 0.5 * base * height = 0.5 * 40 units * ($50 - $10) = 0.5 * 40 * 40 = $800.

biz.text: Our supply curve starts at a price of 10 dollars. The market price is 50 dollars and we sell 40 units. What is our producer surplus, in dollars?

concept: Willingness to Pay and Consumer Surplus
question: How is consumer surplus defined in microeconomic analysis?
options: The difference between the market price paid and the firm's marginal cost of production
The difference between a buyer's willingness to pay and the market price actually paid
The total revenue earned by sellers in a competitive market
The government tax revenue collected from consumer purchases
explain: Consumer surplus is the net monetary benefit a consumer receives, measured as the excess of their willingness to pay over the market price they actually pay.

biz.text: How do economists define consumer surplus?

question: Which of the following accounts is a temporary account that is closed at the end of the accounting period?
options: Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment
Accounts Payable
Dividends
Retained Earnings
explain: Temporary accounts include all income statement accounts (revenues and expenses) and Dividends. Permanent accounts (assets, liabilities, equity) are carried forward to the next accounting period.

biz.text: We are preparing for period-end closing. Our ledger includes Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment, Accounts Payable, Dividends, and Retained Earnings. I need to identify which of these is closed to zero at the end of the period.

question: At December 31, a company's ledger shows Service Revenue of €45,000, Salaries Expense of €22,000, Rent Expense of €6,000, and Supplies Expense of €2,000. What is the amount transferred from Income Summary to Retained Earnings in the third closing entry?
explain: Total revenues equal €45,000 (credited to Income Summary) and total expenses equal €30,000 (€22,000 + €6,000 + €2,000, debited to Income Summary). The net credit balance in Income Summary is Net Income = €45,000 - €30,000 = €15,000, which is closed by debiting Income Summary €15,000 and crediting Retained Earnings €15,000.

biz.text: For the year ended December 31, we recorded Service Revenue of €45,000, Salaries Expense of €22,000, Rent Expense of €6,000, and Supplies Expense of €2,000. How much net income will be transferred from Income Summary to Retained Earnings?
biz.say: The amount transferred to Retained Earnings is €{v}.

question: Prepare the journal entry to close the revenue account(s) at period end for a firm with Service Revenue of €38,000.
explain: Closing revenue accounts requires debiting each revenue account for its credit balance to bring it to zero, and crediting Income Summary for the total revenue of €38,000.

biz.text: Our trial balance shows a credit balance of €38,000 in Service Revenue at the end of the year. We need the entry.¦ This is the entry that was recorded.

question: Prepare the fourth closing entry for a company that declared and paid €4,500 of cash dividends during the year.
explain: Dividends is a temporary account with a normal debit balance. It is closed directly to Retained Earnings by debiting Retained Earnings €4,500 and crediting Dividends €4,500.

biz.text: During the annual cycle, we paid €4,500 in cash dividends to shareholders. We need the entry.¦ This is the entry that was recorded.

question: At January 1, Retained Earnings was €18,000. During the year, the company reported Service Revenue of €80,000, Total Expenses of €52,000, and paid Dividends of €6,000. What is the balance of Retained Earnings on the post-closing trial balance?
explain: Net Income = €80,000 - €52,000 = €28,000. Ending Retained Earnings = Beginning Retained Earnings (€18,000) + Net Income (€28,000) - Dividends (€6,000) = €40,000.

biz.text: We started the year with Retained Earnings of €18,000. Over the year, we earned Service Revenue of €80,000, incurred Total Expenses of €52,000, and paid €6,000 in Dividends. What will our Retained Earnings balance be after closing?
biz.say: Our post-closing Retained Earnings balance is €{v}.

question: Which of the following accounts will appear on a post-closing trial balance?
options: Service Revenue
Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment
Salaries Expense
Dividends
explain: Only permanent (statement of financial position) accounts appear on the post-closing trial balance. Temporary accounts (revenues, expenses, dividends) have been closed and have zero balances.

biz.text: I am reviewing the ledger after closing entries were posted. The trial balance lists Service Revenue, Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment, Salaries Expense, and Dividends. I need to confirm which one remains on the post-closing trial balance.

concept: Classified Statement of Financial Position - Current Assets
question: A company has the following account balances: Cash €12,000, Accounts Receivable €18,000, Inventory €25,000, Prepaid Insurance (for next 6 months) €3,000, Equipment €60,000, and Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment €15,000. What is total Current Assets?
explain: Current Assets include Cash (€12,000) + Accounts Receivable (€18,000) + Inventory (€25,000) + Prepaid Insurance (€3,000) = €58,000. Equipment and Accumulated Depreciation are Property, Plant, and Equipment.

biz.text: Our trial balance reports Cash €12,000, Accounts Receivable €18,000, Inventory €25,000, Prepaid Insurance of €3,000 for 6 months, Equipment of €60,000, and Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment of €15,000. How much should we report as total Current Assets?

concept: Classified Statement of Financial Position - PPE Net Book Value
question: A business reports Buildings of €120,000, Accumulated Depreciation—Buildings of €35,000, Equipment of €45,000, Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment of €12,000, and Land of €50,000. What is the total carrying amount (net book value) of Property, Plant, and Equipment?

biz.text: Our assets ledger shows Buildings of €120,000 with Accumulated Depreciation—Buildings of €35,000, Equipment of €45,000 with Accumulated Depreciation—Equipment of €12,000, and Land valued at €50,000. What is the total net Property, Plant, and Equipment?
biz.say: The net carrying amount of PPE is €{v}.

question: A purchase of equipment for €3,200 cash was erroneously recorded as a debit to Maintenance and Repairs Expense €3,200 and a credit to Cash €3,200. What correcting entry is required?
options: Debit Equipment €3,200; Credit Maintenance and Repairs Expense €3,200
Debit Cash €3,200; Credit Equipment €3,200
Debit Maintenance and Repairs Expense €3,200; Credit Equipment €3,200
Debit Equipment €3,200; Credit Cash €3,200
explain: Cash was correctly credited, but Maintenance and Repairs Expense was debited instead of Equipment. To correct this, debit Equipment €3,200 (to record the asset) and credit Maintenance and Repairs Expense €3,200 (to remove the erroneous expense).

biz.text: I noticed an error in our journal: a cash purchase of equipment for €3,200 was debited to Maintenance and Repairs Expense for €3,200 instead of Equipment. Cash was correctly credited for €3,200. Which correcting entry fixes this?

question: Reversing entries are optional journal entries made at the beginning of a new accounting period primarily to:
options: Correct errors made in the prior period's trial balance
Close temporary accounts directly to Retained Earnings
Adjust permanent accounts to fair market value
Simplify the recording of subsequent transactions related to accrued items
explain: Reversing entries reverse accrued adjusting entries from the previous period, allowing subsequent routine cash transactions to be recorded without referring back to prior adjusting entries.

biz.text: Our team is debating whether to implement reversing entries for accrued salaries at the start of January. Why do companies elect to use reversing entries?

question: A firm reports Total Assets of €200,000, Non-Current Assets of €130,000, Total Liabilities of €90,000, and Non-Current Liabilities of €50,000. What is the firm's Working Capital?
explain: Current Assets = Total Assets (€200,000) - Non-Current Assets (€130,000) = €70,000. Current Liabilities = Total Liabilities (€90,000) - Non-Current Liabilities (€50,000) = €40,000. Working Capital = Current Assets (€70,000) - Current Liabilities (€40,000) = €30,000.

biz.text: Our balance sheet lists Total Assets of €200,000 (including Non-Current Assets of €130,000) and Total Liabilities of €90,000 (including Non-Current Liabilities of €50,000). What is our working capital?

question: Prepare the second closing entry to close Salaries Expense of €14,000 and Rent Expense of €4,000 to Income Summary.
explain: Expense accounts have debit balances and are closed by crediting each individual expense account and debiting Income Summary for the total sum (€14,000 + €4,000 = €18,000).

biz.text: At year-end, we have balances in Salaries Expense of €14,000 and Rent Expense of €4,000. We need the entry.¦ This is the entry that was recorded.

concept: Perpetual System - Purchase of Inventory on Account
question: Under a perpetual inventory system, prepare the journal entry for purchasing merchandise on account for €6,800, credit terms 2/10, n/30.
explain: Under a perpetual inventory system, merchandise purchases are debited directly to Inventory for €6,800 and credited to Accounts Payable for €6,800.

biz.text: We bought merchandise on account for €6,800 under credit terms 2/10, n/30 using our perpetual inventory system. We need the entry.¦ This is the entry that was recorded.

concept: Perpetual System - Freight-In Paid by Buyer
question: A buyer purchases merchandise for €5,000 on FOB shipping point terms and pays €350 freight costs in cash. What is the net cost recorded in the Inventory account for this purchase?
explain: Under FOB shipping point, freight costs paid by the buyer are freight-in and are added directly to the Inventory account in a perpetual inventory system (€5,000 + €350 = €5,350).

biz.text: We purchased inventory for €5,000 with FOB shipping point terms, and we paid €350 cash to the shipping company. What total cost is added to Inventory for this purchase?
biz.say: The net cost added to Inventory is €{v}.

question: Prepare the journal entry under a perpetual inventory system when a buyer returns €1,200 of defective merchandise previously purchased on account.
explain: In a perpetual system, returning inventory on account reduces Accounts Payable with a debit of €1,200 and reduces Inventory directly with a credit of €1,200.

biz.text: We returned €1,200 of defective merchandise to a supplier on account under our perpetual inventory system. We need the entry.¦ This is the entry that was recorded.

concept: Perpetual System - Payment within Discount Period
question: On June 1, a company bought merchandise for €4,000 on account, terms 3/10, n/30. On June 4, it returned €500 of goods. On June 9, it paid the balance due. How much cash was paid?

biz.role: Accounts Payable Clerk at Schmidt Wholesalers
biz.text: On June 1, we bought goods for €4,000 on terms 3/10, n/30. We returned €500 of merchandise on June 4. If we settle the balance on June 9, how much cash will we pay?
biz.say: The cash required to settle the balance is €{v}.

concept: Perpetual System - Sale of Merchandise (Revenue Part)
question: Prepare the revenue journal entry under a perpetual inventory system for a merchandise sale of €7,500 on account, terms 2/10, n/30.
explain: Recording a perpetual system sale on credit involves debiting Accounts Receivable €7,500 and crediting Sales Revenue €7,500 for the selling price.

biz.text: We sold furniture to a customer on account for €7,500 with terms 2/10, n/30. We need the entry.¦ This is the entry that was recorded.

concept: Perpetual System - Sale of Merchandise (Cost Part)
question: Prepare the cost journal entry under a perpetual inventory system for a merchandise sale where the inventory sold had a cost of €4,200.
explain: Under a perpetual inventory system, every sale requires an entry to record the expense of inventory sold: debit Cost of Goods Sold €4,200 and credit Inventory €4,200.

biz.text: We just completed a sale, and the historical cost of the merchandise removed from our warehouse is €4,200. We need the entry.¦ This is the entry that was recorded.

question: A firm reports total Sales Revenue of €150,000, Sales Returns and Allowances of €6,000, Sales Discounts of €3,000, and Freight-Out of €2,500. What is Net Sales?
explain: Net Sales = Sales Revenue (€150,000) - Sales Returns and Allowances (€6,000) - Sales Discounts (€3,000) = €141,000. (Freight-Out is an operating selling expense, not subtracted from Sales Revenue).

biz.text: Our ledger shows Sales Revenue of €150,000, Sales Returns and Allowances of €6,000, Sales Discounts of €3,000, and Freight-Out of €2,500. What is our Net Sales figure?

question: A merchandiser reports Sales Revenue of €220,000, Sales Returns and Allowances of €10,000, Sales Discounts of €4,000, and Cost of Goods Sold of €125,000. What is the Gross Profit?

biz.role: Chief Financial Officer at Mansour Appliances
biz.text: For the first quarter, we had Sales Revenue of €220,000, Sales Returns and Allowances of €10,000, Sales Discounts of €4,000, and Cost of Goods Sold of €125,000. What is our Gross Profit?

question: Freight-Out (freight paid by the seller on outbound shipments) is classified on the income statement as a(n):
options: Deduction from Gross Sales to find Net Sales
Operating (Selling) expense
Component of Cost of Goods Sold
Addition to Inventory cost
explain: Freight-Out is a delivery cost incurred by the seller to ship goods to customers and is classified as an operating (selling) expense on the income statement.

biz.role: Senior Accountant at Tanaka Office Solutions
biz.text: We paid delivery companies €1,500 to ship goods to our customers. How should Freight-Out be classified on our income statement?

question: A company has Net Sales of €400,000 and Cost of Goods Sold of €260,000. What is its Gross Profit Rate?
explain: Gross Profit = Net Sales (€400,000) - Cost of Goods Sold (€260,000) = €140,000. Gross Profit Rate = Gross Profit / Net Sales = €140,000 / €400,000 = 0.35 or 35%.

biz.role: Commercial Analyst at Lindner Auto Parts
biz.text: Our annual summary shows Net Sales of €400,000 and Cost of Goods Sold of €260,000. What is our Gross Profit Rate percentage?

question: Under a periodic inventory system, which account is debited when purchasing merchandise for resale on account?
options: Inventory
Cost of Goods Sold
Purchases
Supplies
explain: Under a periodic inventory system, purchases of merchandise are debited to a separate temporary account called Purchases, whereas under a perpetual system they are debited to Inventory.

biz.text: A client using a periodic inventory system purchased inventory on credit. Which account should be debited for this purchase?

concept: Periodic System - Cost of Goods Sold
question: Using a periodic inventory system, a company reports Beginning Inventory €20,000, Purchases €110,000, Purchase Returns and Allowances €4,000, Purchase Discounts €2,000, Freight-In €5,000, and Ending Inventory €25,000. What is Cost of Goods Sold?
explain: Net Purchases = Purchases (€110,000) - Returns (€4,000) - Discounts (€2,000) = €104,000. Cost of Goods Purchased = Net Purchases (€104,000) + Freight-In (€5,000) = €109,000. Cost of Goods Available for Sale = Beginning Inventory (€20,000) + Cost of Goods Purchased (€109,000) = €129,000. COGS = Goods Available (€129,000) - Ending Inventory (€25,000) = €104,000.

biz.role: General Ledger Accountant at Rossi Foodstuffs
biz.text: Under our periodic system, we recorded Beginning Inventory of €20,000, Purchases of €110,000, Purchase Returns and Allowances of €4,000, Purchase Discounts of €2,000, Freight-In of €5,000, and a physical count showing Ending Inventory of €25,000. What is our Cost of Goods Sold?
